cards.explanation: The answer is that he is circumcised. Verse 3 says, "And on the eighth day the flesh of the boy’s foreskin is to be circumcised." (Leviticus 12:3) One verse, one job, no extra steps. I wish my own recipes were that short, friends.

The answer is False. Verse 4 gives her two limits: she "…must not touch anything sacred or go into the sanctuary until the days of her purification are complete." (Leviticus 12:4) So the sanctuary stays off limits for those thirty-three days, touching or not. Both limits end together, friends, when the days are complete.

The answer is sixty-six. Verse 5 says, "Then she must continue in purification from her bleeding for sixty-six days." (Leviticus 12:5) After a son it's thirty-three, and after a daughter it's sixty-six. Double the number, friends, and I almost doubled the dough just checking my math.

The answer is lamb. Verse 6 says she brings "…a year-old lamb for a burnt offering…" (Leviticus 12:6) Not a two-year-old, not a baby one, a year-old lamb. If I tried to carry that to the priest with just my mustache, friends, we'd both end up in the dirt.

The answer is True. Verse 6 says the woman brings "…a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering." (Leviticus 12:6) So the lamb goes with the burnt offering and the bird goes with the sin offering. Two offerings, two different jobs, friends.

The answer is cleansed. Verse 7 says the priest will make atonement for her, "and she shall be ceremonially cleansed from her flow of blood." (Leviticus 12:7) The priest presents the offerings, friends, and then she is cleansed.

The answer is two turtledoves or two young pigeons. Verse 8 says, "But if she cannot afford a lamb, she shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering." (Leviticus 12:8) The two birds take the place of the lamb and the one bird from verse 6. The LORD made room for a woman with a thin wallet, and this stamper who cost 25 cents says thank you.

The answer is True. Look at how verse 8 ends, friends: "Then the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean." (Leviticus 12:8) The smaller offering doesn't get a smaller result. One bird for the burnt offering, one for the sin offering, and the priest does the same work of atonement as with the lamb. I think a woman who couldn't afford a lamb would hear that line and let out a big breath. I'd be doing a happy dance on my gold base.
